clue.text: Newcastle far away? Block saying how far

parts.note: a place far away is miles to go, read here as 'miles to' with the destination following
Newcastle upon Tyne lies in the north-east of England, abbreviated NE

explanation.surface: Someone asks whether Newcastle is far off, and points to a roadside stone that tells the distance.
explanation.walkthrough: Newcastle is the city in north-east England, so the question 'Newcastle far away?' becomes 'miles to NE'.
explanation.definitionFit: A roadside stone marker carved with the distance to a town is exactly a block saying how far.

clue.text: One having child's body preserved

definitions.meaning: a mother, in the nursery word
an embalmed corpse wrapped in bandages, as in ancient Egypt

explanation.definitionFit: The word is both a child's name for mother and an embalmed Egyptian corpse.

clue.text: Trees concealed by poplar and chestnut

indicators.note: the trees are concealed by the words that follow, so their surrounding letters are stripped away to reveal them

explanation.surface: Some trees are hidden among the poplars and chestnuts.
explanation.walkthrough: The answer is not one unbroken run: it is the tail of 'poplar' joined to the start of 'chestnut', with 'and' between them skipped, so POP, AND and TNUT are what is stripped away.
explanation.definitionFit: Larches are deciduous conifers, a kind of tree.

clue.text: Dirt from sink found on barrel

indicators.note: in a down clue, the first piece sits on top of the second

parts.note: to scuttle a ship is to sink it deliberately
a butt is a large cask

explanation.surface: Grime from the kitchen sink is found on a barrel.
explanation.definitionFit: Dirt in the sense of gossip or rumour, originally sailors' chat around the water cask.

clue.text: Gas produced by cattle, extremely gusty, rising in their stomach?

indicators.note: the cattle hold the other letters in their middle

parts.note: oxen are cattle

indicators.note: in a down clue, rising reads the letters upward, so backwards
only the extremes of the word, its first and last letters, are used

explanation.surface: Wind produced by cows, extremely gusty and coming up from their stomachs.
explanation.definitionFit: The element O is a colourless gas essential for breathing.

clue.text: Come specially round church house, to see this artwork?

indicators.note: the shuffled letters go around the others
arranged specially, so the letters are set out in a new order

parts.note: CE is the Church of England

explanation.surface: An invitation to come round to a church house to view a picture.
explanation.walkthrough: 'specially' rearranges the first word into ECMO. CE is the Church of England.
explanation.definitionFit: Latin for 'behold the man', it is the title of many paintings of Christ crowned with thorns.

clue.text: Simple container for water, not quite cold

indicators.note: not quite the whole word, so its final letter is dropped

parts.note: a basin is a bowl that holds water
C is the abbreviation for cold, as on taps

explanation.surface: A plain water bowl that is not quite cold.
explanation.definitionFit: Basic and simple are synonyms for plain, elementary, without frills.

clue.text: Don't allow pop group to finish early

indicators.note: stopping early means the last letter is not reached

parts.note: a band is a pop group

explanation.surface: A parent refuses to let a pop group stop early.
explanation.definitionFit: To ban is to prohibit or forbid.

clue.text: Son, grown up, a chilly figure

parts.note: a boy grown up is now a man

explanation.surface: A son, now an adult, is a cold, distant presence.
explanation.definitionFit: A figure built from snow in winter is literally chilly.

clue.text: Always quarrelling, plenty of these in a fall

definitions.meaning: a ... life is one of constant fighting

definitions.text: plenty of these in a fall
definitions.meaning: heavy rain is said to pour down cats and dogs

explanation.definitionFit: The phrase describes a quarrelsome relationship, and the creatures said to fall in a downpour.

clue.text: Poisonous element drunk a little, and another element swallowed

indicators.note: one piece takes the other into its middle, as if gulping it down

parts.note: slightly tipsy is merry
copper, chemical symbol Cu

explanation.surface: A tipsy drinker has swallowed something toxic along with another chemical.
explanation.definitionFit: Quicksilver, the liquid metal, is a toxic chemical element, symbol Hg.

clue.text: A reason not to arrange for a wife, maybe

parts.note: a con is an argument against, as in pros and cons
to sort is to put in order

explanation.surface: Someone finds an excuse not to set up a match for a woman.
explanation.definitionFit: A spouse, especially of a monarch, is a consort; a wife is one example.

clue.text: Defiant expression, rejecting fodder

indicators.note: rejecting throws the word back, so it is read from the end

parts.note: hay is dried grass fed to animals

explanation.surface: Someone scornfully refuses animal feed with a rude noise.
explanation.definitionFit: A jeering exclamation of contempt or defiance, like 'boo' or 'yah boo sucks'.

clue.text: Film a particular fielder

definitions.meaning: the 1949 Carol Reed thriller set in Vienna, starring Orson Welles
in cricket, a fielding position behind the batsman on the off side, near the boundary

explanation.definitionFit: The title names both a classic British thriller and a cricket fielding position.

clue.text: One that fixes a sort of lock, say, in a stiff condition

indicators.note: say signals that the words are spoken, giving similar sounds

parts.words: One that fixes a sort of lock
parts.note: a rigger is one who fixes rigging, and a mortise is a sort of lock

explanation.surface: A locksmith fits a type of lock while in a stiff condition.
explanation.definitionFit: The stiffening of the muscles after death is a rigid bodily state.

clue.text: Ring belonged to woman briefly

indicators.note: cut short, so the last letter goes

parts.note: it belonged to a woman: it was hers

explanation.surface: A ring that once belonged to a woman.
explanation.definitionFit: A flat ring of metal or rubber used under a nut or bolt is this.

clue.text: Finished getting prepared for the cold

definitions.meaning: a job concluded is said to be completed and tied up
dressed warmly in plenty of layers

explanation.definitionFit: The phrase means both concluded and bundled up warmly against winter weather.

clue.text: Thought I was digging to bury silver

indicators.note: one word buries the other, holding it inside

parts.note: mined means dug for ore
Ag is the chemical symbol for silver

explanation.surface: A prospector thought they were digging to hide silver.
explanation.definitionFit: Imagined and thought are both past tenses of supposing or fancying something.

clue.text: Unexpected visitor rattled tin — not so polite

indicators.note: rattled as in shaken about, so the letters fall into a new order

parts.note: ruder means less polite

explanation.surface: A caller shakes a collection tin rather rudely.
explanation.definitionFit: An intruder is a trespasser or uninvited person who arrives unannounced.

clue.text: Worker encloses fine channel: that's a bit rich

indicators.note: one word surrounds the others, holding them inside

parts.note: the worker ant is a crossword staple
F is the abbreviation for fine, as on pencils
a flue is a duct or passage for smoke

explanation.surface: An employee boxes in a decent channel, which someone thinks is a bit much.
explanation.walkthrough: 'a bit rich' looks like the idiom for cheek, but it means wealthy.
explanation.definitionFit: Affluent means wealthy or well off, which is to say rather rich.

clue.text: Flourish; if cooler, manage

parts.note: a fan cools you down
to fare is to get on or manage

explanation.surface: A flourish of advice: if you have a cooler, you'll manage.
explanation.definitionFit: A flourish of trumpets announcing someone is a fanfare.

clue.text: Clearing out, not started, is pressing

indicators.note: the word has not started, so its first letter is lost

parts.note: purging means emptying or cleansing out

explanation.surface: A clear-out that is pressing yet hasn't started.
explanation.definitionFit: Pressing and urging both mean pushing someone insistently.

clue.text: Beard's not a hazard

indicators.note: not having it means the following letter is taken away

parts.note: an imperial is a small pointed beard below the lower lip

explanation.surface: Someone insists that a beard poses no danger.
explanation.definitionFit: To hazard something is to put it at risk, to endanger it.

clue.text: Ancient criminal gaoled

indicators.note: criminal as in crooked, so the letters are bent into a new order

explanation.surface: An elderly lawbreaker has been locked up.
explanation.definitionFit: Something age-old has existed for a very long time, so is ancient.

clue.text: One option drunk when taking in the cricket?

definitions.text: One option drunk when taking in the cricket?

indicators.note: the shuffled letters take another word into their middle
drunk as in made tipsy, so the letters reel into a new order

parts.note: a grig is an old word for a cricket or grasshopper
the Roman numeral for one is I

explanation.surface: A spectator chooses a glass of wine to drink while watching the cricket.
explanation.walkthrough: 'drunk' rearranges OPTION into PINOTO. A grig is an old dialect word for the insect, not the sport, which the surface suggests.
explanation.definitionFit: A popular dry white Italian wine is one choice of drink a spectator might have.

clue.text: One found among the pages of Dickens

definitions.text: One found among the pages of Dickens

indicators.note: one letter is placed in the midst of the others

parts.note: PP is the abbreviation for pages
the Roman numeral for one is I

explanation.surface: Someone spots a single character somewhere in a Dickens novel.
explanation.walkthrough: The whole clue also describes the hero of Great Expectations, a figure met in the novelist's pages.
explanation.definitionFit: Philip Pirrip, the orphan narrator of Great Expectations, is a character in the novelist's book.

clue.text: Girl like her father?

definitions.meaning: read as pop plus -py: like pop, her dad

explanation.definitionFit: It is a girl's name, and playfully reads as resembling one's pop, or father.

clue.text: Died in apparent poverty, not going willingly?

parts.note: D is the abbreviation for died, as in genealogies
ragged means in tattered clothes, looking poor

explanation.surface: Someone died looking destitute, and reluctant to go.
explanation.definitionFit: Someone hauled along against their will has been pulled forcibly rather than walking freely.

clue.text: Ted would be very disappointed with this paunch

indicators.note: the name plus this piece would make the longer word, so taking the name away leaves the piece

parts.note: gutted is British slang for bitterly disappointed
taken as written, the name

explanation.surface: Ted would be dismayed to see his own pot belly.
explanation.walkthrough: This is a reverse-style clue: adding TED to the answer makes GUTTED, British slang for bitterly disappointed, so the answer is GUTTED without TED.
explanation.definitionFit: A gut is a protruding belly, a pot belly.

clue.text: To produce a larger harvest, perhaps, a sudden occurrence

definitions.text: To produce a larger harvest, perhaps
definitions.meaning: to outdo another grower in yield
an outbreak or sudden appearance of something

explanation.definitionFit: The word reads playfully as a verb for out-yielding, and as a noun for a sudden emergence.

clue.text: Fold paper lengthways at first, and stuff into mouth

parts.note: P is the abbreviation for paper

indicators.note: only the opening letter of the word is taken

parts.note: to eat is to put food into the mouth

explanation.surface: Someone folds paper lengthwise, then crams it into their mouth.
explanation.definitionFit: A pleat is a doubled-over crease in fabric, a kind of fold.

clue.text: Not the first show of colour spread out about one

indicators.note: the two words sit around another, enclosing it

parts.note: red is a colour
to splay is to spread out
the Roman numeral for one is I

explanation.surface: A colourful display spread out around one thing, not for the first time.
explanation.definitionFit: To show again, a repeat exhibition, is a second showing rather than the first.
